newsitem.title: UK: CU up as broker repeats "buy" advice.
newsitem.headline: CU up as broker repeats "buy" advice.

text.p: Shares In Commercial Union rose again on Tuesday as UBS reiterated its "buy" recommendation on the stock, traders said.
Commercial Union, subject of much bid speculation in the press in recent days, added 11p to 688-1/2p. The shares have risen over 13 percent since October 4.
The latest rumour circulating is that Dutch bank ABN AMRO may be poised to make a bid for all or part of the company.
But UBS analyst Chris Hitchings played down such talk.
"The press seem to think there's been a lot of bid talk. there hasn't. We're fundamental buyers," said Hitchings.
"In a difficult market background it remains the best managed stock and in a difficult market background that's usually the one you want to have," said UBS analyst Chris Hitchings.
Paribas also dismissed talk linking ABN AMRO with Commercial Union, describing it as "clearly ridiculous" and advising taking advantage of the short term hype to switch into cheaper stocks.

ABN AMRO, said Paribas, was unlikely to make the necessary rights issue at a price/earnings (PE) of 12 times to pay twice net worth for mature cyclical businesses on a price/earnings ratio of 18 times.

Paribas attributed the recent spike in the share price to a recent analyst visit to Commercial Union's operations in France sparking a flurry on buy notes on the company and wrong footing market-makers.
It suggested switching into B.A.T where, it said, "unrealistic" litigation fears had created real value on even a worst case scenario.
